{{Quote|Even life-forms without midi-chlorians and cellular structures, such as the fractal urchins of Protogeyser, can touch its energy.|An excerpt from ''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'' by Jedi biologist Bowspritz, discussing the ability of animals to touch the Force|<ref name="TJP" />}}
'''Protogeyser''' was an astronomical object<ref name="TJP" /> located in the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim's]] [[Protogeyser system/Legends|Protogeyser system]].<ref name="Atlas Appendix" /> Known to the wider [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] by the [[Ruusan Reformations/Legends|Ruusan Reformation]] of [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], the [[fractal urchin]]s, a [[Sentience/Legends|non-sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] that lacked cellular structures and thus [[Midi-chlorian/Legends|midi-chlorians]],<ref name="TJP" /> life-forms that lived symbiotically inside cells and allowed their symbiont to detect [[The Force/Legends|the Force]],<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref> originated from Protogeyser. This distinction earned the fractal urchins, along with Protogeyser, a mention in the "Galactic Bestiary" section of the [[Jedi Initiate/Legends|Jedi trainee]] [[Book/Legends|guidebook]] ''[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force]]'', where the [[Jedi Biologist|Jedi biologist]] [[Bowspritz]] used the species as an example of animals that were connected to the Force despite their lack of midi-chlorians.<ref name="TJP" />

==Behind the scenes==
Created by author [[Daniel Wallace]], Protogeyser was first mentioned in the [[2010]] reference book [[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']].<ref name="TJP" /> In [[2012]], the Online Appendix of ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' at [[StarWars.com]] placed the Protogeyser [[Star system/Legends|system]], and therefore Protogeyser itself, in grid square K-8.<ref name="Atlas Appendix" />
